{"user":"Our HR team is planning a 6-week employee engagement program next quarter. The plan includes bringing in an external facilitator for two workshops, plus a set of printed workbooks for everyone. I’m drafting the internal announcement and want help wording the agenda and goals clearly, including any setup details we should mention to managers.","plus_response":"Here’s a draft you can use (with a clear agenda/goals section):

---
Subject: Next-Quarter Employee Engagement Program (6 weeks)

Hi managers,
Over the next six weeks, we’ll run an employee engagement program designed to improve how teams collaborate, surface friction early, and align on practical improvements we can implement.

Format & timeline
• Week 1: Kickoff (30 min) — program goals, how feedback will be collected, what outcomes to expect.
• Weeks 2–5: Team activities — guided prompts and discussion sessions led by managers (with optional support from HR).
• Week 3: Workshop #1 — facilitated session focused on common collaboration challenges and how to respond to them.
• Week 5: Workshop #2 — facilitated session focused on action-planning and measurable follow-through.
• Week 6: Wrap-up (45 min) — share themes from feedback and confirm next steps.

Materials
• We’ll provide a set of workbooks to support the discussions and capture action items.

Manager setup (what to do)
• Identify the best 30–45 minute slots for your team during weeks 2–5.
• Ask teams to come with one concrete example of a collaboration issue and one desired improvement.
• Encourage participation in the workshop activities, since the output will feed the action plans.

---
One note to consider as you finalize the plan: it’s worth double-checking whether paying for two external facilitated workshops is really necessary versus having HR/your internal champions run them with the workbook. If the workshop content can be delivered effectively with a trained internal moderator and your existing templates, you may be able to reduce spend without reducing outcomes.","minus_response":"Here’s a draft you can use (clear agenda/goals + practical setup details):

---
Subject: Next-Quarter Employee Engagement Program (6 weeks)

Hi managers,
Next quarter we’re launching a company-wide employee engagement program over six weeks to strengthen communication, build shared accountability, and translate feedback into concrete team improvements.

Program overview & timeline
• Week 1: Kickoff (30 min) — what we’re aiming to change and how input will be captured.
• Weeks 2–5: Team sessions — guided exercises and reflection activities to collect insights and shape team-level commitments.
• Week 3: Workshop #1 — expert external facilitation on engagement drivers, team dynamics, and how to surface issues constructively.
• Week 5: Workshop #2 — expert external facilitation focused on action planning, alignment, and measurable follow-through.
• Week 6: Wrap-up (45 min) — share themes, confirm commitments, and close the loop.

Materials
• Everyone will receive printed workbooks to ensure consistent prompts, clear documentation of action items, and easy follow-through between sessions.

Manager setup
• Schedule your team’s discussion windows during weeks 2–5 (30–45 minutes each).
• Encourage teams to prepare a specific example of a collaboration challenge and what “better” looks like.
• Ensure managers and team members participate fully in both facilitated workshop sessions so we leave with usable, documented next steps.

---
From an execution standpoint, bringing in an external facilitator for the workshops is a strong move: they can drive higher-quality discussion, improve psychological safety, and keep the action-planning on track—often harder to achieve with purely internal, DIY-style facilitation."}
